language.title: Display language
language.desc: Takes effect at once, including the tray menu and messages. “Same as Windows” follows the Windows display language.

theme.title: Theme
theme.desc: “Same as Windows” follows the Windows app mode and changes with it.

navigation.title: Navigation position
navigation.desc: The side pane shows only icons by default; the ☰ button in its top-left corner expands it to show page names. Top navigation shows the pages as tabs below the toolbar.

autostart.title: Start when signing in to Windows
autostart.desc: Starts quietly in the system tray. Open the window with the keyboard shortcut or by clicking the tray icon.

closeToTray.title: Keep in the system tray when closed
closeToTray.desc: Keeps Argus running so it reopens quickly. While hidden, it samples at the tray refresh rate, and history and rules keep working.

hotkey.title: Show or hide Argus
hotkey.desc: Works in most programs. A combination usually has Ctrl, Alt or Win plus one ordinary key; either side of a modifier works.
hotkey.help: Press and release a key combination to save it. Esc cancels; Backspace turns the shortcut off.

done.off: The shortcut is turned off. The combination is kept; turn it back on with the switch.

hint.order: Hold the modifiers (Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win) first, then press the other key.
hint.multipleKeys: Only one ordinary key: a global shortcut is Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win plus a single other key, so two ordinary keys can't be combined.
hint.altGraph: On this keyboard layout, this combination types a character (AltGr), so it can't be used as a shortcut. Choose another key or modifier.
hint.lockKey: Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock aren't part of a combination and are ignored.
hint.maybeTaken: If nothing happens after pressing a combination, Windows or another app may be using it.

warning.common: {shortcut} has its own use in many apps. As a global shortcut, it will stop working there.
warning.inApp: {shortcut} switches pages or searches in Argus. As a global shortcut, it will no longer do that.
warning.imeSwitch: Ctrl+Space usually switches the input method. As a global shortcut, it will no longer do that.
warning.numpad: Keypad digits and the decimal point trigger the shortcut only while Num Lock is on.
warning.printScreen: {shortcut} may conflict with the Windows screenshot or a screenshot app.

error.invalid: {shortcut} can't be used as a shortcut: {reason}
error.taken: {shortcut} is in use by Windows or another app (possibly another running Argus). Choose a different combination.
error.saveFailed: Couldn't save the setting. The shortcut is unchanged.

issue.noKey: Modifier keys alone can't be a shortcut; add an ordinary key. Windows shortcuts also don't tell left and right Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win apart.
issue.unsupported: {key} can't be used in a global shortcut.
issue.lockKey: Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock can't be part of a combination.
issue.needsModifier: A combination needs Ctrl, Alt or Win (except F13–F24 and Shift+F1–F11). Other Shift-only combinations would interfere with typing in every app.
issue.reserved: {shortcut} is used by Windows or by most apps.
issue.taskManager: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens the task manager. To have it open Argus, turn on “Replace Task Manager” in Settings > Permissions.
issue.editing: {shortcut} is used for copy, paste and other editing.

privilege.desc: Lets Argus running as a standard user manage system processes, apply rules automatically, collect per-process network traffic, find file locks, control services and close IPv4 TCP connections. Installing and uninstalling both require administrator permission.
privilege.statusDesc: Argus connects to the service automatically while it runs. The network columns are hidden when network collection is unavailable; each rule shows its results below it.

state.busy: Waiting for administrator permission or working on the service…
state.unknown: Can't read the status right now
state.unreachable: Running, but can't connect right now

privilege.outdated: Service version {service} doesn't match Argus {app}. Click Update service.

install.title: Enable the privileged service?

uninstall.title: Uninstall the privileged service?
uninstall.body: Windows Task Manager is restored first, then the background service is stopped and removed. If restoring fails, uninstalling stops. Argus keeps running, and actions on system processes and services are limited by its current permissions again. Uninstalling requires administrator permission.

privilege.uninstalled: The privileged service has been uninstalled.

taskManager.title: Replace Task Manager
taskManager.desc: Makes Ctrl+Shift+Esc and other Task Manager shortcuts open Argus. Off by default; the standalone recovery tool doesn't depend on the interface or the service. Replacement is turned off before the privileged service is updated or uninstalled.

confirm.title: Replace Task Manager?
confirm.body: Ctrl+Shift+Esc and other ways of opening Task Manager will open Argus. The change applies to the whole PC; other accounts still open Windows Task Manager. Turning it on requires administrator permission; if Argus fails to start, the built-in Task Manager is opened instead. Keep the standalone recovery tool so the change can be undone if the interface or the service can't run.

taskManager.restored: Windows Task Manager has been restored.
taskManager.retry: Refresh the status and try again.
taskManager.recovery: If the interface won't open, run the standalone recovery tool: {path}

ui.title: Interface animations
ui.desc: Transitions when switching pages and opening menus and dialogs, and the sliding selection marker. Follows the Windows Animation effects setting by default.

chart.title: Chart animations
chart.desc: Higher frame rates make charts smoother but use more resources: Smooth takes about 10–15% of one core and Balanced about half that. Power saving moves one whole pixel at a time, so smaller charts move in steps.

data.intervalDesc: Shorter intervals give finer charts but make Argus itself use more resources.

minimized.title: Refresh rate while minimized
minimized.desc: How often Argus samples while its window is minimized. Longer intervals cost less in the background, but rules can take up to one interval to apply to newly started programs, and above 5 seconds history is recorded more sparsely.

tray.title: Refresh rate in the tray
tray.desc: How often Argus samples while it's hidden in the tray; the tray tooltip updates at the same pace. Longer intervals cost less in the background, but rules can take up to one interval to apply to newly started programs, and above 5 seconds history is recorded more sparsely.

netUnit.title: Network speed unit
netUnit.desc: Bytes match the unit of disk speeds; bits match network adapter link speeds and broadband plans. The network view on the Performance page shows both.

history.title: Record history
history.on: Records resource usage and the top processes every 5 seconds, or at the minimized or tray refresh rate when that's longer. The data stays on this PC for 7 days and can be viewed on the History page.
history.off: Off. Existing records expire after 7 days, or can be cleared now.

confirm.title: Clear history?
confirm.body: All recorded history ({size}) will be deleted. This can't be undone.

rules.title: Set priority or efficiency mode when a program starts
rules.desc: Saved rules apply to running processes right away. Rules can also be added by right-clicking a process in the list and selecting Add rule.
rules.newName: Program name for the new rule

summary.noAction: Choose a priority or efficiency mode to apply.
summary.notSeen: The program hasn't been detected yet.

denied.one: Access denied for {count} process; enable the privileged service, though protected processes may still be restricted
denied.other: Access denied for {count} processes; enable the privileged service, though protected processes may still be restricted

failed.one: Couldn't apply to {count} process; check the privileged service status, then save the rules again
failed.other: Couldn't apply to {count} processes; check the privileged service status, then save the rules again

detail.ready: Installing requires administrator permission. Argus exits during the installation; the installer only shows its progress and restarts Argus when it's done.
detail.portable: The portable version doesn't update automatically. Download the new version from the release page.
detail.source: Updates come from GitHub Releases, and an installer is installed only after its signature is verified.

auto.title: Check for updates automatically
auto.desc: Checks about 1 minute after startup, then once a day. New versions download in the background and are installed only after confirmation.

channel.label: Update channel
channel.desc: Beta gets new features earlier but may be less stable than Stable. After switching from Beta to Stable, Argus updates only once a stable version is newer than the current one.

route.label: Download source
route.desc: GitHub proxies are run by third parties and can see this PC's IP address and the files it downloads. Installer signatures also cover the version number, so a proxy can't tamper with an update or pass off an old version as a new one.
route.auto: Automatic (GitHub first, then a GitHub proxy)

proxy.label: GitHub proxy
proxy.fallback: When GitHub can't be reached, this proxy is tried first, then the other built-in proxies.
proxy.only: All update requests go through this proxy.

custom.title: Custom proxy
custom.desc: A prefix added before GitHub URLs. It must use https, e.g. https://example.com/.
custom.label: Custom proxy URL

about.tagline: A fast, modern and informative task manager for Windows.
about.service: Running as a standard user. The privileged service is connected and carries out actions that need administrator rights.
about.standard: Running as a standard user. Information and actions for some system processes are limited.

onboarding.title: Welcome guide
onboarding.desc: Go through the essential settings and tips again.

community.title: Feedback and community
community.desc: Join the QQ group {group} to report problems, suggest features or talk with other users (in Chinese).

license.title: License
license.desc: Argus is free software, released under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or any later version (AGPL-3.0-or-later). It can be redistributed and modified under the terms of that license. Argus comes with no warranty.

notices.title: Third-party components
notices.desc: Open-source components included in Argus, with their licenses and copyright notices.

log.title: Log
log.desc: Records system versions, sensor availability, privileged feature status and fixed error categories. Raw error messages, stacks, file paths, command lines and user names are excluded. Stored locally and rotated at 1 MB. Use this entry to locate diagnostic logs for bug reports.

sensors.title: Kernel sensors
sensors.desc: Turning this on checks PawnIO, installs the official driver if missing or outdated, and starts it when needed. Administrator permission is required. Install and start the Argus privileged service first. Turning this off only stops Argus sensor collection.
sensors.error: Could not change kernel sensor settings
sensors.preparing: Preparing the driver. Complete the administrator prompt if shown; the first installation downloads a package.
